# dsh-sidebar-tags

**Colored session tags for the DeepSeek Harness sidebar.** Tag any session from
its own row, see the

tag at a glance, and filter your whole history by tag from
a dedicated sidebar panel.
中文说明 · Changelog · MIT
## Why

A long-running Harness install turns into hundreds of sessions across several
workspaces. The sideba

r can show them, search them and archive them, but there
is no way to say *"this one is a client del

iverable"* or *"come back to this on
Friday"* — and no way to get those sessions back as a set.
This plugin adds exactly that layer, and nothing else:

| **Tags on the row** | A colored dot (plus `+n`) at the start of the session row |
| **Tag from the

row** | An entry in the row's "…" menu and a hover button, both a one-click picker |
| **Tag on hov

er** | The hover card lists the session's tags and its note |
| **Tag panel** | A sidebar panel: per
-tag counts, one-click filtering, full-text search over titles and notes, jump to session, create/re
name/recolor/delete tags, export/import a backup |

It is a pure client-side plugin: no host routes, no files outside the browser, no
model-facing conte

nt, no changes to any shipped Harness file. Data lives in
`localStorage` and can be exported as JSON

## Use

1. Hover a session row and click the tag button, or open the row's **…** menu and
use **Tag this ses

sion…**.
2. Pick one or more tags. The row gets a colored dot immediately.
3. Open **Session tags**

in the sidebar to see counts per tag, filter the list,
search titles and notes, and manage the tag s

et itself.
4. Tags are stored per browser profile. Use **Export a backup** in the panel to
keep a co
py, and **Import a backup** to bring it to another browser.

Six tags ship with the plugin (To do / Doing / Important / Reference /
Archivable / Idea); all of th

em can be renamed, recolored or deleted, and new
ones can be created in the panel.
## Compatibility
| Harness | Status |

| `0.2.0-rc.2` | tested (see "How this was verified") |
| `0.2.0-rc.1` | expected compatible (same s

lot contract) |
| older lines | the plugin stays dormant and logs nothing; the seats it needs did no

act) |
| older lines | the plugin stays dormant and logs nothing; the seats it needs did not exist |

The plugin contributes only to seats the shell declares
(`sidebar.panellist`, the keyed `main`, `sid

ebar.session.row.leading`,
`sidebar.session.row.hover`, `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item`,
`sid

ebar.workspaces.session.row.action`) and every registration goes through
`ctx.slots.inject`. A shell

without a seat never runs the callback, so a future
Harness that renames a seat degrades to "this o

ne feature is missing" instead of
breaking the boot.
### Known limits

- **The row dot is a resting-state marker.** The host renders
`sidebar.session.row.leading` only whi

le a row's primary state is idle; a row
that is running, waiting for approval or carrying an unread

completion shows
the host's own status dot there instead. The tags are still visible in the
hover ca

rd, the row menu and the panel.
- **`localStorage` is per browser profile.** Clearing site data clea

the Harness** may leave a record behind; the panel
prunes records for sessions the host no longer li

sts the next time it opens.
- The panel lists the sessions the current page knows about, plus rememb

ered
titles for tagged sessions that are no longer loaded.
## How this was verified

Everything below is runnable from a checkout with plain Node (no bundler, no
network):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`scripts/verify-browser.mjs <gui-url>` drives a headless Chromium over the
DevTools protocol against

a live instance and asserts that the stylesheet is
injected, the panel row exists, selecting it mou

nts the panel, and the panel
renders — useful in CI with a browser available. `lab/index.html` (serv

ed by
`node tools/serve.mjs`) renders the same bundle in a stand-in shell so the UI can
be inspected
without installing anything.
State that has actually been observed, not just intended:

- the loader mounts the plugin from a profile `link:` install, and the host
serves `dsh-sidebar-tags

the four row/panel components, the store and the projections are covered by
the unit tests at the l
evel of registration contract and pure functions.

Not yet observed: a click-through of the rendered panel inside a real Harness
window. The environmen

t this plugin was written in had no browser that could
start (sandbox) — that check is the first thi

ng to run on a normal desktop, and
`scripts/verify-browser.mjs` automates it.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Panel data comes from the Harness' own Cordis stores (`sessions.list`,
`uiSession.sessionStatus`, `w

orkspaces.list`) read through `getSnapshot()` and
`subscribe()` — the same observables the shipped s

idebar reads, so no extra
polling, RPC or duplicate cache exists.
### Why no build step

`lib/client.js` is hand-written CommonJS wrapped in the one call the Harness
loader expects:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The only module it requires is `react`, which every shell provides. That means
the published artifac

t is the source: a checkout is installable and reviewable
as-is, `git diff` shows behaviour, and the

re is no toolchain to trust or keep
current. `scripts/build.mjs` replaces a bundler with a structura

l check —
wrapper shape, bundle id versus package name, patch row versus package name,
region index

versus file body, and syntax. The trade-off is no TypeScript and no
tree-shaking, which a plugin of

this size does not miss; if that changes, the
module boundaries are already laid out as `@region` se

ctions for a move to
`tsdown`.
